text.p: June T-bond futures will rely on key support around the 106-00 area on Monday to put a stop to their descent since January, technical analysts said.
Several support factors step in around here, including old lows and a major retracement target from weekly continuation charts. Friday's low at 106-12 would first have to give way.
"We're looking for 106-12 to come under pressure today," Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said.
T-bonds were quoted at 106-19 at 1006 GMT in automated trade, down 1/32 from Friday's settlement in Chicago.
Analysts said the 106-00 area was crucial.
The futures hit a low of 106-02 low on June 14, 1996 a 105-28 low on July 12 and a 106-00 low on September 6 on weekly continuation charts.

Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London also noted on Reuters Financial Television 106-00 represents a 61.8 percent retracement of the late 1994 to early 1996 rally. That took the market from a 96-01 low in November 1994 to a 122-04 high on January 5, 1996 on weekly charts.
Miller saw support nearby at 105-27,25 from, Elliott Wave extention targets.

Analysts said if the market managed to plough through all that, then the September 5 low for the June contract at 105-20 would give some support. Miller said 105-18 equated to a yield of 7.25 percent on the long bond.
On the upside, Miller said the overnight high of 106-23 would likely cap any upward move. Above there, 107-03 would act as resistance coming from the April 10 low and the middle of the recent range.
Trendline resistance then comes in at 107-17, analysts said.
September Eurodollar futures settled at 99.665 in Chicago on Friday, droping from a high of 93.750 and nearing support at 93.630 from the April 1 low.
